verdict.reasoning: Headache location and timing match: patient says, “I keep having a headache… It's on the left side at the back” and onset “started yesterday.”
Onset and build are described as: “About mid-morning” and “it kind of built up gradually… over a short period of time.”
Character and severity match: “quite, intense, and kinda quite throbbing” and pain score “I'd say about eight.”

No diurnal or positional pattern: patient reports “No, it hasn't made any difference, the time of the day” and to lying/standing/bending/coughing/sneezing: “Um, no.” Valsalva-related changes not explicitly named but coughing/sneezing addressed.

Patient denies these associated symptoms: to nausea/vomiting “No, nothing,” to blurred vision or pain over eyes “No,” and to funny lights/problems with light “No, no.” Aura and photophobia are encompassed by denial of funny lights and problems with light.
Neurologic and systemic negatives are documented: to tingling/numbness/weakness “No, nothing,” to fevers/shivery/sweaty “No, no fever,” and to rashes “No.”
Intake and sleep are confirmed: “have you been eating and drinking OK?” – “Yes, yes, like normal” and “did you manage to sleep through the night OK?” – “Uh, yes I did.”
Lack of prior headaches and that this is unusual are stated: patient says, “it's unusual for me, to have a headache” and later, to past headaches, “Not really.”
Impact on function without missed work: to missed work – “Uh, no,” but adds, “I'm finding it really hard to, to do any of, my work, or, normal things.”
Blood pressure recency addressed: doctor asks, “have you had your blood pressure checked?” patient replies, “Um, no, not recently.”
No past medical history: “have you got any other medical problems?” – “Um, no I haven't.”
No regular medications: Doctor asks, “Anything you take medication for?” – “No I don't.”
Ibuprofen use and lack of relief documented: “I took some… Nurofen, yesterday” and to effect, “Not really.”

Allergies are inquired about (“any over-the-counter medications or allergies?”) but the patient only answers about Nurofen/Ibuprofen and does not explicitly deny allergies; ‘No allergies reported’ adds information not stated.
Family history stated: “my mother's had hypertension, and she does get migraines.”
Living situation and job are documented: lives with “My partner” and works as “I'm a designer.”
Substance use documented: “do you smoke at all normally?” – “No I don't.” “Do you drink any alcohol regularly?” – “No.” “any other drugs?” – “No.”

Summary matches: unilateral throbbing left posterior headache (“left side at the back… throbbing”), acute since yesterday, first episode (“Not really” prior headaches; “unusual for me”), no red-flag features (no fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, neuro deficits, rash), and family history of migraines (“she does get migraines”).
Plan to use an alternative NSAID with food: “trying a slightly stronger, pain relief… similar to Ibuprofen, but taking instead of Ibuprofen… and taking that regularly with food.”
Concurrent paracetamol is allowed: “You can take Paracetamol along with that.”
Advice given: “Try and um, take rest, have lots of good hydration.”

Safety-net instructions match: seek care if “the pain's getting worse, or you get new symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness… or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing, then we need to speak to you.”

Follow-up timeframe given: “if it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two. Then certainly give us a call back, if, when you've tried the medication that I've prescribed from the pharmacy.”
